sourceCopy.name: Effect Size Calculator
sourceCopy.title: Effect Size Calculator Free | UsefulVerse
sourceCopy.description: Calculate Cohen’s d and Hedges’ g from two independent groups’ means, standard deviations and sample sizes. Free and local.
sourceCopy.intro: Enter summary statistics for two independent groups to calculate their signed standardized mean difference, pooled standard deviation and small-sample corrected Hedges’ g.
sourceCopy.howQuestion: What does an effect size calculator measure?
sourceCopy.howAnswer: It expresses the difference between two group means in pooled standard-deviation units. Cohen’s d is the uncorrected standardized difference; Hedges’ g applies a small-sample correction.
sourceCopy.privacyAnswer: No. The calculation runs in this browser. Your summary statistics are not sent to a server or saved by this tool.
howTo: Enter each group’s mean, sample standard deviation and sample size.
Select Calculate to see the signed Cohen’s d and Hedges’ g.
Review the pooled-SD assumption and copy the results if useful.

example.label: Load example: means 105 and 100, SD 10, n 25 each

fields.designNote: For independent groups, this version uses the conventional pooled-SD definition and assumes a shared population variance. Enter sample (n−1) standard deviations, not standard errors.
fields.accuracyNote: Each sample size must be 2–1,000,000; means and SDs are limited to ±1,000,000,000 (SDs cannot be negative). At least one SD must be above zero.
fields.formulaNote: d = (mean₁ − mean₂) / pooled SD. Hedges’ g = J(df) × d, with df = n₁ + n₂ − 2. The sign depends on group order. A magnitude is not automatically “small”, “medium” or “large”; interpret it in the subject area and study design.

messages.copyUnavailable: Copy is unavailable in this browser.
messages.inputRange: Enter finite values within the supported range.
messages.sampleSize: Sample sizes must be whole numbers from 2 to 1,000,000.
messages.zeroVariance: At least one group must have non-zero standard deviation.
messages.resultRange: The result exceeds the supported numeric range.

additionalFaqs.question: What is the difference between Cohen’s d and Hedges’ g?
additionalFaqs.answer: Both standardize the mean difference by a pooled standard deviation. Hedges’ g multiplies d by a small-sample correction, which reduces bias when samples are small.

additionalFaqs.question: Can I enter standard errors instead of standard deviations?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. This calculator expects each group’s sample standard deviation. A standard error describes uncertainty in a sample estimate and is not interchangeable with the SD here.

additionalFaqs.question: Does a larger effect size prove that a result is important?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. Effect size describes a standardized difference, not statistical significance, causation or practical importance. Context, uncertainty, study design and the measurement scale matter.
